documents.name: okafor2019

metadata.title: Shared Gauges and the Dry Season

documents.text:
Rivers that cross three borders keep their own counsel. No single ministry can speak for the water, and no treaty has yet persuaded a flood to wait for a signature.

The basin agreements of the last century treated the river as a line on a map. They divided the flow by volume and the banks by sovereignty, and they assumed that what was measured at the gauge was what the farmers downstream would receive.

The survey of eleven agreements finds the opposite. Where the gauges were shared, the disputes were settled in the commissions; where each state kept its own records, the disputes were settled by the dry season.

documents.name: lindqvist2021
documents.text:
An archive is a promise made to a reader who has not yet been born. The clerk who files a letter cannot know which sentence will matter, and so the whole letter is kept.

The reading rooms of three municipal archives changed in the years after their catalogues went online. Requests for whole boxes fell by half while requests for single folios doubled, because readers had learned to ask for the page they already knew they wanted.

documents.name: harbour-notes
documents.text:
Tuesday. The ferry ran late again, and the harbour master blamed the tide tables, which were printed in a year when the channel was deeper.

Wednesday. Forty-one gulls stood on the breakwater at noon and none at dusk.
